documents.text: The v1 study adapts a pretrained predictive model using unlabeled target inputs, without source examples. Its objective reduces predictive entropy and its adjustable components are feature-wise affine modulations. Experiments concern image/digit classification. The method discussion explicitly also allows compatible probabilistic regressors with predictive variance; therefore 'entropy adaptation is categorically impossible for regression' misstates this source. That observation does not automatically provide a distribution or useful entropy objective for a deterministic scalar regressor. Claims of benefit remain scoped to the source's evaluated settings.
documents.title: Fully Test-time Adaptation by Entropy Minimization

documents.text: Test-time training jointly prepares a main prediction task and an auxiliary self-supervised task sharing a feature extractor. At deployment the auxiliary loss updates shared parameters using unlabeled input. Rotation prediction is the image-specific example, not a universal requirement. Standard per-instance and stateful online variants differ in whether updates are retained. The paper gives a convex-model discussion involving gradient alignment; this is not an unconditional guarantee of improvement for any auxiliary task. The preparation stage and availability of a suitable self-supervised task differ from adapting an arbitrary off-the-shelf checkpoint.
documents.title: Test-Time Training for Out-of-Distribution Generalization

documents.text: SHOT studies source-free unsupervised domain adaptation for classification: retain the trained classifier while adapting a target feature extractor without source examples. Information maximization combines confident individual predictions with diversity across the target collection; self-supervised pseudo-label refinement is another component. Its setting is not identical to one-pass adaptation of a scalar regressor. Class probabilities, class diversity and pseudo-label definitions must be distinguished from continuous regression outputs. The source is evidence that source-free adaptation is already studied, not proof that all source-free tasks are solved.
documents.title: Do We Really Need to Access the Source Data? Source Hypothesis Transfer for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation

documents.text: This study replaces source-estimated batch-normalization statistics with statistics from unlabeled corrupted target images. It evaluates classification robustness under explicit adaptation access conditions, including how many similarly corrupted examples are available together. Such access differs from an isolated query or a changing mixed stream. No new classification entropy objective is required for this statistics-based baseline. Observed gains on common-corruption benchmarks do not establish that every distribution shift or regression target benefits from moment adjustment.
documents.title: Improving robustness against common corruptions by covariate shift adaptation

documents.text: Deep CORAL penalizes differences between source and target feature covariance matrices while learning deep representations. Its training setup combines labeled source data and unlabeled target data, unlike deployment with only a source model. The covariance-matching objective gives prior art for feature-distribution alignment but does not by itself establish a source-free deployment procedure or guarantee preservation of a regression function. The paper also situates covariance matching among related distribution-alignment approaches; alignment is not a novel concept merely because used in a new proposal.
documents.title: Deep CORAL: Correlation Alignment for Deep Domain Adaptation

documents.text: Batch normalization normalizes activations using mini-batch statistics and learns a scale and offset per activation channel. Training and inference statistics must be distinguished. This is architectural and optimization background, not itself evidence of successful target-domain adaptation. The source attributes its training benefits to reducing internal covariate shift; a survey should distinguish that source's interpretation from an established universal explanation or a guarantee under external distribution shift.
documents.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift

documents.text: This classification calibration study distinguishes prediction confidence from empirical correctness, reports miscalibration in modern networks, and evaluates post-processing methods such as temperature scaling. Calibration fitting uses a labeled validation set, unlike label-free target adaptation. It is useful background against equating confidence with correctness, but is not a direct experiment on adaptation of deterministic regression models. Neither calibration quality nor increased confidence alone establishes improved target regression error.
documents.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks

documents.text: Domain-adversarial learning trains representations to support labeled-source prediction while reducing a domain classifier's ability to distinguish source and target examples. A gradient-reversal component implements the adversarial update. The study uses source examples and unlabeled target examples during training, so it is not directly a source-free test-time method. Domain indistinguishability and task-discriminative structure play different roles. This broader adaptation prior art is relevant for comparing information assumptions, not proof of feasibility under stricter deployment constraints.
documents.title: Domain-Adversarial Training of Neural Networks

selection: Core adaptation methods plus broader architecture/calibration/domain-alignment background; not a target-paper-only reference list
